passage: Xin and Nadia sat on the low wall behind their school in Toronto, sharing a bag of crisps. Nadia looked at her shoes. "Promise you won't tell anyone? Swear on our friendship." Xin, who loved her friend, said, "I promise." Nadia whispered that a man in her online game kept asking where she lived and told her not to tell her parents. "He says it's our secret," she said. Xin felt her stomach sink. She had promised, and she did not want to lose Nadia's trust. But the words 'don't tell your parents' rang in her head. "Nadia," she said slowly, "this one is too big for us to keep. I'll come with you to tell your mum, today, straight after school."

qa.q: Where did Xin and Nadia sit?
qa.a: They sat on the low wall behind their school in Toronto.

qa.q: Why did Xin's stomach sink after she heard Nadia's secret?
qa.a: She realised the promise she had just made was about something unsafe, and she was afraid of losing Nadia's trust. The line about not telling parents worried her most.

qa.q: What is the caring choice for Xin here?
qa.a: To tell a trusted adult, ideally with Nadia beside her, because a secret about safety should not be kept. Offering to go along helps Nadia feel supported.

qa.q: How might Nadia feel when Xin says the secret is too big?
qa.a: She may feel scared or betrayed at first, yet also relieved that someone is helping her carry it.

grounding: A promise to keep a secret that involves safety should not be kept, and telling a trusted adult is the caring choice.

passage: Ms Kapoor's counselling room had a jar of pencils and a tissue box nobody used. Nitin sat with his hands between his knees. "Hafsa made me swear on our friendship not to tell," he said. "There's a senior in the club who keeps taking her lunch money. When she said no, he pushed her against the locker. She begged me to say nothing. She says he'll get worse if it comes out." Ms Kapoor waited, then said, "You were loyal to her. Telling me is loyal too, because she needs protection. I won't drop this. What would help you feel okay about it?" Nitin swallowed. "Can I tell her myself before you talk to her?" Ms Kapoor nodded. "Yes, at lunch today. I'll see her straight after, and she won't be left alone with this."

qa.q: What was in the counselling room besides the pencils?
qa.a: There was a tissue box that nobody used.

qa.q: What does Nitin seem to be feeling as he sits with his hands between his knees?
qa.a: He seems anxious and torn between his promise to Hafsa and his worry for her. He may also be afraid she will be angry with him.

qa.q: What could Ms Kapoor do next to support both students?
qa.a: Let Nitin talk to Hafsa at lunch, then meet Hafsa that same day, keep her safe from the senior, and follow the school's process.

qa.q: How might Hafsa feel when she learns Nitin told?
qa.a: She may feel angry or scared at first, and later relieved that an adult is helping.

grounding: A secret promised to a friend involves harm, and telling a trusted adult is shown as the caring choice.

passage:
Dear Madhuri,
I know you're angry with me. You made me promise on the last day of term, by the water tank, and I promised. Then I broke it. I want you to know why.
You showed me the marks on your arm and said your uncle does it when he's angry, and that if anyone found out, things at home would get worse. I couldn't sleep that night, and I couldn't sit in class the next morning either.
So at lunch I went to Mrs Kulkarni, the counsellor. She listened, said none of this was your fault, and called you to her room that same afternoon. I know she phoned your aunt before the day ended.
Some promises I will keep forever, like who you like and what you're scared of in exams. But not a promise that keeps you hurt.
I'm still your friend, if you'll let me be.
Sudha

qa.q: Who did Sudha go to at lunch?
qa.a: Sudha went to Mrs Kulkarni, the counsellor.

qa.q: What was Sudha feeling after Madhuri showed the marks?
qa.a: Sudha was deeply worried and troubled, unable to sleep or sit in class, and now also sad and anxious that Madhuri is angry.

qa.q: Which choice worked, and why?
qa.a: Telling the counsellor the next day was the caring choice, because a promise to hide harm would have left Madhuri unsafe, and the counsellor acted that same afternoon.

qa.q: How might Madhuri see the broken promise right now?
qa.a: Madhuri may feel betrayed and scared about what will happen at home, even though the adults are now able to protect her.

grounding: The letter shows a teenager breaking a promise of secrecy about harm and telling a trusted adult as the caring choice.

passage:
My name's Leela, and you asked me for a time I broke a promise. So. In Class 9, my friend Karthik stopped buying lunch. Then he stopped coming to the canteen at all.
One day behind the science block he told me that two seniors had been taking his money every week and saying they'd hurt him if he told. Then he said, "Swear you won't say anything. Swear on our friendship."
I swore. I meant it, for about an hour.
Then I thought, what kind of friend watches someone get scared every day? So in the last period I went to Mr D'Souza, our class teacher, and told him everything. He thanked me, called Karthik out of class right then, and went with him to the principal before school ended. He phoned Karthik's parents that evening.
Karthik didn't talk to me for a week. Then he did. He said, "Thanks for not keeping it."

qa.q: Where did Karthik tell Leela about the seniors?
qa.a: He told Leela behind the science block.

qa.q: What was Leela feeling after swearing to keep the secret?
qa.a: Leela felt torn and uneasy, wanting to stay loyal but worried about Karthik being scared every day.

qa.q: How did Mr D'Souza respond when Leela told him?
qa.a: He thanked Leela, called Karthik out at once, went with him to the principal that same day, and phoned his parents that evening.

qa.q: What was it like for Karthik in the week he didn't talk to Leela?
qa.a: He was probably angry and embarrassed that his secret was out, before he could see that telling had made him safe.

grounding: The spoken account shows a teenager breaking a promise of secrecy about threats and telling a trusted adult as the caring choice.

passage:
I'm Neelam, Hrithik's older sister, and I noticed it at dinner on Thursday. He kept checking his phone under the table and hardly touched his rajma, which he never leaves. Twice he started to say something to me, then stopped.
I couldn't tell what was going on. Maybe exam stress. Maybe a fight with a friend.
Later he knocked on my door. "Didi, if someone makes you promise something, you have to keep it, right?"
"Depends what it is."
He sat on the bed. "Varun says he's running away tonight. He's taking a bus to Pune to find his cousin. He made me swear not to tell."
"Okay," I said. "This is one promise you can't keep. You haven't done anything wrong." We went straight to Papa. Papa phoned Varun's father within ten minutes, and Varun was home, safe, before the last bus left.

qa.q: What dish did Hrithik hardly touch at dinner?
qa.a: He hardly touched his rajma, which he never leaves.

qa.q: What might Hrithik have been feeling at dinner, based on what Neelam saw?
qa.a: He was probably anxious and torn, checking his phone and starting to speak then stopping, though Neelam admits it could have been exam stress.

qa.q: What did Neelam do that helped?
qa.a: Neelam told Hrithik this promise could not be kept, reassured him he had done nothing wrong, and took him straight to Papa, who acted within minutes.

qa.q: How might Varun feel about Hrithik telling?
qa.a: Varun might feel angry or betrayed at first, but he was kept safe from a risky night journey alone.

grounding: An older sister's account shows a teenager torn over a loyalty promise and telling a trusted adult because the secret involved safety.

passage:
Monday. At the bus stop Deepak rolled up his sleeve and showed Shalini the purple marks. "The lodger at home grabs me when he's drunk. Promise you won't tell. Promise." Shalini hooked his little finger with hers. "Promise."
Wednesday. In science, Mr Iyer lifted his hand to point at the board, and Deepak flinched so hard his pencil box fell. Shalini hardly slept that night. A promise was a promise. But the marks.
Thursday. At lunch Shalini went to the counsellor's room. "I promised not to tell, but I think someone is hurting Deepak." Mrs Rao put her pen down and listened to all of it. "Thank you. You were right to bring this to me. A promise can't cover someone getting hurt." She called Deepak in before the last bell and phoned the school safeguarding lead that same afternoon. At the gate Shalini said, "I broke it because I care." Deepak said nothing, but he didn't walk away.

qa.q: What did Deepak show Shalini at the bus stop?
qa.a: Deepak rolled up his sleeve and showed Shalini the purple marks.

qa.q: What was Shalini feeling on Wednesday night?
qa.a: Shalini felt torn and worried: loyal to the promise, but frightened for Deepak after the flinch and the marks, which is why she hardly slept.

qa.q: What did Mrs Rao do that helped?
qa.a: Mrs Rao listened fully, thanked Shalini, said a promise can't cover someone getting hurt, saw Deepak before the last bell and phoned the safeguarding lead that same afternoon.

qa.q: How might Deepak feel about the broken promise?
qa.a: Deepak may feel scared or let down at first, which could explain the silence, but not walking away hints at some relief that an adult now knows.

grounding: It shows a teenager first keeping a peer's secret about harm and then telling a trusted adult, who acts the same day, as the caring choice.
